description: CallState is one call as the server sees it. Replace-by-id on upsert.

^(can_transfer_to_application)$.description:
can_transfer_to_application is server-computed: true for inbound calls and
 taken callbacks (source == CALL_SOURCE_CALLBACK), false otherwise. Plain
 outbound calls must not be offered application (IVR module) transfer
 targets — forwarding them into a queue module strands the agent.
 Clients gate the "App" transfer-target segment on this
 flag instead of re-deriving the rule from direction/source themselves.

^(conversation_id)$.description:
conversation_id is the platform conversation this leg belongs to
 (`conversationId` on the platform's call; the same id the call reporting
 API carries). Transfer and conference legs carry their parent call's
 conversation id, so it is the stable key across leg swaps. Empty until a
 push names it.

^(customer_number)$.description:
customer_number is the external party's number, whatever the direction:
 the customer leg's `from` on an inbound call, its `to` on an outbound one;
 else the number of the one live non-agent member of this call's
 conference. Never an agent's own number and never the SIP INVITE's From,
 so it stays the customer's across transfers, where `from`/`to` follow the
 leg. Empty when nothing names the customer. Set once and not cleared.
 A caller who withheld their number is NOT filtered out: the field carries
 whatever number the platform sent for the customer leg (on an inbound call
 the same value as `from`), and `anonymous` says it was withheld. A client
 that hides a withheld number must hide this field too.

^(handed_over)$.description:
handed_over is true once the agent in `invited_by` has left and this agent
 is alone with the customer: a completed transfer, warm or cold, as opposed
 to a colleague who added this agent and is still on the call. Latches true.
 The platform does not record why the inviter left, so an inviter whose line
 dropped reads the same — for the receiver that is the same outcome.

^(invited_by)$.description:
invited_by is the agent who brought this agent onto the call: the colleague
 who transferred it (blind or after a consult) or added this agent to a
 conference. On the receiving side these are one and the same leg — a
 transfer started in babelConnect reaches the target as a conference invite
 (source CALL_SOURCE_CONFERENCE) — so the field is named for what is known,
 not for the intent. Read from the conference push, decided once on the
 first push that shows this agent's own member still ringing (`pending`)
 and no other agent member still joining (`pending`): set only when exactly
 ONE other agent member is `added` then, never overwritten. A push where
 another agent is still joining decides nothing, since that agent may be the
 inviter. After such a wait the agent is named only if it was the one agent
 seen joining and nobody joined beside an agent already `added`; anything
 else may be a fellow invitee and names nobody. Unset when that is
 not decidable (no conference push, a reload after the invite, this agent
 answering while another agent was still joining, two or more agents
 already in the call): absent rather than wrong.

^(webrtc_reoffer)$.description:
webrtc_reoffer is an SDP offer for a FRESH media leg on a call that is
 already answered. The server sets it when a session takes over an answered
 call from another one (a reloaded window reclaiming it from the call grace
 window, or a takeover hand-off), because the previous window's peer
 connection is gone. A client that holds no media for the call answers it
 with AnswerCall{call_id, sdp}, without ringing and whatever its auto-answer
 setting; a client that already holds a leg for the call ignores it. Cleared
 once answered, or after about 30s unanswered (the server then releases the
 leg, answer_failed after). Never on a RINGING call, which uses webrtc_offer.
